title: Content item
description: One piece of content (a weapon, spell, class, playbook, template, …): mechanics only, one file per item. Player-facing text lives in the pack's i18n files under keys derived from the item ID (`<id>.name`, `<id>.description`). An item either defines new content (`id` + `type`) or overrides another pack's item (`override`), changing only the properties it mentions.

id.description: Local content ID, permanent and never reused. Must match the file path: `content/weapons/longsword.yaml` holds `weapons.longsword`.

type.description: A content type declared by this pack or a dependency, or the built-in `template`.

override.description: Homebrew: the ID of another pack's item to override. Only the properties given here change.

extends.description: A permanent variant: inherit everything from this item, then apply the properties given here.

removeTags.description: Templates only: tags the copy's item doesn't have. A copy's `item.tags` are the base item's, then for each template in order its `removeTags` taken away and its `tags` added; a later template may add a removed tag again.

fields.description: Values for the item fields declared by the content type. How a value is read depends on the declared type: `integer`, `decimal`, `boolean` and `dice` values are formulas (a plain literal is a formula with no inputs); `string`, `enum` and `id` values are literal strings; `set` values are lists of literals. A template may set the rules' `templateFields` and the fields of the content type its `appliesTo` names; its values are merged into the copy's `item` in template order, replacing the base item's, and its formulas see the base item as `base`. A template may give `null` for a field: the field is absent from the copy's `item` (no declared default applies), unless a later template sets it again. Only templates may give `null`. A template's `string`, `enum` or `id` value may be `{ formula }`: a string formula read as its numeric values are (with `base`, `prior` and `params`), so a kept template takes a damage type from its keeper's `params`; a result that isn't a string, or isn't one of an enum's values, leaves the field as it was. Only templates may give `{ formula }`.

params.description: Templates only: values the template's item fields read as `params.<name>`, given by the content keeping it (`keepsTemplates` `params`). A param the keeper doesn't give, or on a saved template, is its `default`, else absent.

state.description: Extra per-copy state keys this item (or template) adds to the character's copy, beyond those its content type declares.

computed.description: Computed values on this item's copies, added to the content type's or replacing one of them by name. A template's are added to the copies it is applied to.

followUps.description: Follow-ups that apply while the character has this item's copy or pick, as effects do. Their formulas see `item` and `self`.

grants.description: Other content this item makes active on the character while it is active itself, e.g. class features at level N. A grant with `scope: applied` applies while the item is the source of an active applied entry: the granted content is applied content too, with the entry as `self`.

immuneTo.description: Applied content the character can't be affected by while this item is active: an `applied` entry whose source matches is blocked and reported as the rules issue `immune`.

reapply.description: What applying this item again does, replacing its content type's `reapply`.

nameFrom.description: A string state key whose value names each copy of this item (a custom stunt the player names), replacing its content type's `nameFrom`. While the copy's value of the key is a non-empty string, it is the copy's name (computeSheet's `copyNames`).

standardCopies.description: Content every character holds a copy of while this item is active, e.g. a playbook's own gear: queries that read only `item`, resolved by loadRuleset. Each match is a standard copy with the instance ID `<pack>-<local ID>`, the colon and dots as hyphens; the character file saves it only once it differs from its defaults.

keepsFields.description: Item fields the templates this item keeps (`keepsTemplates`) leave as they are, on the copies it keeps them on: a specific magic weapon's Price, which already counts the runes it comes with. A template the player applies later changes them as usual.

keepsTemplates.description: Templates this item keeps while it is active: on the character's copies (`copies`), each copy of `copies.type` whose base item matches `copies.where` has the template applied after its saved ones; on content picked or granted to the character (`content`), each item of `content.type` matching `content.where` has the template's fields and tags merged into its `item`. A query reading only `item` is resolved by loadRuleset; one that also reads the keeper is an activation condition. A template whose `appliesTo` doesn't match isn't kept. Nothing is saved.

prerequisites.description: Conditions for having this item. Failing ones are rules issues (`prerequisite-not-met`), never blocking unless strict mode is on.

repeatable.description: The item may be picked more than once (a feat taken again): exclusivity groups (a choice's `unique`) don't apply to it, so a pick of it in one choice of a group leaves it eligible in the others, and isn't `already-picked`. Default false.

appliesTo.description: Templates only: the items this template may be applied to: one query, or several, any of which may match. With several, the template's item fields are the template fields and those every listed type declares; its formulas see `item` as the first type's.

suppress.description: IDs of the content type's effects this item switches off.

item.description: The content granted: an ID; `{ formula }`, a string formula evaluated as an activation condition is (it reads `self`, `item` and input fields) to a content ID, qualified in the grant's pack as a literal one is; an empty string grants nothing, and an ID that names no content grants nothing with the sheet error `unknown-id`. So content grants what the player named in its state (a spell picked for the day). Or `{ query }`: every content item of the query's type it matches, hidden items left out, in ruleset order, each granted as its own grant; `where` is an activation condition with the candidate as `item` (a query that reads only `item` is resolved at load), so a core grant reaches content an add-on adds.

forEach.description: The grant is made once per element of this list, in list order, with `x` bound to the element in `when`, `item` (a query's `where` too), `state` and `choices`. The list is an activation formula as `when` is (it reads `self`, `item` and input fields; `x` is unbound in it); an empty list grants nothing, and one that fails or isn't a list grants nothing with its sheet error. So one core grant covers every key of a family, an add-on's too: `{ forEach: keysOf('ward'), when: "fieldOf('wards.{ward}', x) > 0", item: { query: { type: rite, where: item.ward == x } } }`.

scope.description: `holder` (default): the grant applies while the content is held, and the granted content is activated as held content. `applied`: while the content is the source of an active, unblocked `applied` entry, the granted content is activated as applied content (its `scope: applied` effects, immunities, grants and actions) with the granting entry as `self`, and immunities block it as they would an entry of it.

waivePrerequisites.description: The granted item's prerequisites don't apply to this activation of it (content that gives a feat outright, whether or not the character meets its prerequisites). Its own grants and picks are checked as usual. Default false.

state.description: State values for the granted content: in place of the owner copy's (a holder grant) or the granting entry's (a grant with `scope: applied`), the granted content sees them as `self.<key>`. Each key is a state key the granted content declares (`unknown-state-key` at load); each value is a formula of the key's type evaluated as an activation condition is (it reads `self`, `item` and input fields). For a holder grant they are the defaults of the granted content's saved state: a value saved in the owner's `grants` wins. A condition that includes a valued condition gives its value: `{ item: conditions.enfeebled, scope: applied, state: { value: 2 } }`.

choices.description: Holder grants: picks the grant makes for the granted content's own choices, by choice ID (a slot's key for a slotted choice). A choice a literal `item` doesn't declare, a literal option it doesn't offer, or `choices` on a grant with `scope: applied`, is `unknown-reference` at load; with a formula `item`, a key the content doesn't declare presets nothing. A preset choice is answered: its picks are these, it is never pending, and `choose` and `unchoose` on it are `preset-choice`. Each pick's `option` is a literal or `{ formula }`, evaluated as an activation condition is, to a content ID (qualified in the grant's pack, as `item` is), an inline option ID or a value; a pick's `choices` preset the picked option's own choices. A formula that fails, or gives neither a string nor a number, leaves its pick out with a `formula-error`. So content gives a feat for a skill it names: `{ item: feats.assurance, choices: { skill: [{ option: skill.athletics }] } }`.

presetTree.description: A grant's preset picks: keyed by the owner's bare choice IDs; each pick's `option` is a literal or `{ formula }`.

id.description: Stable ID; rules issues carry it, and its text is `<owner>.prerequisites.<id>`.

template.description: The template kept on the copies or the content.

copies.description: The copies it is kept on: a content type and a condition over the copy's base item. A condition reading only `item` is resolved by loadRuleset; one that also reads the keeper (`self`, `picksOf`, `character`, input fields, the character functions) is an activation condition with `item` the candidate, so a keeper keeps a template on what its own choice picked.

content.description: The content without a copy of its own it is kept on: every holder activation of content picked or granted to the character whose item is of the type and matches the condition, read as `copies`' is. The template may give only fields and tags (`template-without-copy` otherwise).

params.description: Values for the template's `params`, each a formula of the param's type evaluated as an activation condition is, with the keeper's roots (`self`, `item`, `picksOf`, `character`, input fields). `character.applied` is among them, the saved applied entries with their state, so a param can name the element of an active spell. The template's item fields read them as `params.<name>`, so a kept template scales with the character. A name the template doesn't declare is `unknown-name` at load.

when.description: An activation condition: while it holds, the template is kept.

scope.description: `holder` (default): while the item is held. `applied`: while it is the source of an active, unblocked `applied` entry, on that character's copies.
